import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 5.59

by B. Hartley

Let $G$ be a locally finite group which is the product of a $p$-subgroup and a
$q$-subgroup, where $p$ and $q$ are distinct primes. Is $G$ a $\{p, q\}$-group?

Here a group is locally finite if every finitely generated subgroup is finite.
A $p$-subgroup is a subgroup in which every element has order a power of $p$
(`IsPGroup`). "$G$ is the product of $P$ and $Q$" means $G = PQ$ as sets, i.e.
every element of $G$ is of the form $xy$ with $x \in P$ and $y \in Q$; the
subgroups $P$ and $Q$ need not be normal. A $\{p, q\}$-group is a group in which
every element has order of the form $p^a q^b$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open scoped Pointwise

namespace Kourovka.«5.59»

/-- A group is locally finite if every finitely generated subgroup is finite. -/
def IsLocallyFiniteGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Finite H

/-- Every finite group is locally finite. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyFiniteGroup.of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] :
    IsLocallyFiniteGroup G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/-- Every locally finite group is a torsion group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyFiniteGroup.isTorsion {G : Type*} [Group G] (hG : IsLocallyFiniteGroup G) :
    Monoid.IsTorsion G := by
  intro g
  have : Finite (Subgroup.zpowers g) := hG _ ⟨{g}, by simp [Subgroup.zpowers_eq_closure]⟩
  rw [← orderOf_pos_iff, ← Subgroup.orderOf_mk g (Subgroup.mem_zpowers g)]
  exact orderOf_pos _

/--
Let $G$ be a locally finite group which is the product of a $p$-subgroup $P$ and a
$q$-subgroup $Q$, where $p$ and $q$ are distinct primes, i.e. $G = PQ$ as sets.
Is $G$ a $\{p, q\}$-group, i.e. does every element of $G$ have order of the form
$p^a q^b$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.59» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (p q : ℕ) (P Q : Subgroup G),
      IsLocallyFiniteGroup G → p.Prime → q.Prime → p ≠ q →
      IsPGroup p P → IsPGroup q Q → (P : Set G) * (Q : Set G) = Set.univ →
      ∀ g : G, ∃ a b : ℕ, orderOf g = p ^ a * q ^ b := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.59»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition with the stated reading (universal over G, p, q, P, Q; set product; element-wise p-/q-/{p,q}-group notions) is the natural and standard reading of the problem.
modeling_decisions: Locally finite is defined via finitely generated subgroups in the sense of Subgroup.FG (closure of a Finset), i.e. ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Finite H.

p-subgroup / q-subgroup are formalized with Mathlib's IsPGroup p ↥P (every element of P has p-power order), which is the correct notion for possibly infinite subgroups and matches the decomposition notes.

'G is the product of P and Q' is formalized as the pointwise set product (P : Set G) * (Q : Set G) = Set.univ (open scoped Pointwise); this is exactly ∀ g, ∃ x ∈ P, ∃ y ∈ Q, x * y = g. P and Q are not assumed normal, so the join P ⊔ Q = ⊤ would have been wrong.

'{p,q}-group' is formalized as ∀ g : G, ∃ a b : ℕ, orderOf g = p ^ a * q ^ b. This forces orderOf g ≠ 0, so it is the element-wise notion (every element has order p^a q^b) with no orderOf = 0 loophole; in a locally finite group this is equivalent to every finite subgroup having order p^a q^b.
Primes are ℕ with p.Prime, q.Prime and distinctness p ≠ q as explicit hypotheses; G is quantified in Type as in the other Kourovka files.
answer(True) means 'yes, every such G is a {p,q}-group'; answer(False) means a counterexample exists.

$q$-subgroup, where $p$ and $q$ are distinct primes. Is $G$ a $\{p, q\}$-group?
